q1: SELECT ITEMPRICE.NP, ITM.TYPE, ITM.ITEMNO FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMNO AS ITN, ITP.NP AS NP FROM ITP AS ITP WHERE ITP.NP > 1000) AS ITEMPRICE, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITEMPRICE.ITN = ITM.ITEMNO
q2: SELECT DISTINCT ITP.NP, ITM.TYPE, ITM.ITEMNO FROM ITP AS ITP, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITP.NP > 1000 AND ITP.ITEMNO = ITM.ITEMNO
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ITEMPRICE.NP, ITM.TYPE, ITM.ITEMNO FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ITP.ITEMNO AS ITN, ITP.NP AS NP FROM ITP AS ITP WHERE ITP.NP > 1000) AS ITEMPRICE, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITEMPRICE.ITN = ITM.ITEMNO
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ITP.NP, ITM.TYPE, ITM.ITEMNO FROM ITP AS ITP, ITM AS ITM WHERE ITP.NP > 1000 AND ITP.ITEMNO = ITM.ITEMNO
counterexample: INSERT INTO ITP (ITEMNO, NP) VALUES (1, NULL); INSERT INTO ITP (ITEMNO, NP) VALUES (2, 1500); INSERT INTO ITM (ITEMNO, TYPE) VALUES (1, 1); INSERT INTO ITM (ITEMNO, TYPE) VALUES (2, 2);
explanation: Q1 first filters the ITP table to only include rows where NP > 1000, then performs a join with the ITM table. Q2, on the other hand, performs the join first and then filters the result to only include rows where NP > 1000. This difference in the order of operations can lead to different results if there are NULL values in the NP column of the ITP table.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should include an item in the ITP table with NP = NULL, which will be included in Q1's result but not in Q2's result.
